Proposal for that support should be sent to MoFPI by the states or national level institutions or organizations or partner institutions. 7.5 Eligibility criteria: 7.5.1 The proposals should fulfill the following conditions:- i) The proposal should relate to ODOP; ii) Minimum turnover of product to be eligible for assistance should be Rs 5 crore; iii) The final product should be the one to be sold to the consumer in retail pack; iv) Applicant should be an FPO/SHG/cooperative/ regional - State levels SPV to bring large number of producers together; v) Product and producers should be scalable to larger levels; vi) Management and entrepreneurship capability of promoting entity should be established in the proposal. 7.6 Procedure for applying for assistance under Branding & Marketing 7.6.1 Detailed Project Report preparation: i) A DPR should be prepared for the proposal, comprising essential details

At the National level, National Institute for Food Technology Entrepreneurship and Management (NIFTEM) and Indian Institute of Food Processing Technology (IIFPT) would play pivotal role in capacity building & research. They would be eligible for financial assistance towards research and capacity building. NIFTEM and IIFPT in partnership with State Level Technical Institutions would provide training and research support to the selected enterprises/groups/clusters. National level product specific institutions under ICAR, CSIR or premier institutes like DFRL and CFTRI wi ll be partner institutions for providing support at the vertical level across the country for training and research. 8.1.2 NIFTEM and IIFPT would carry out the following activities: i) Capacity building and training for MoFPI, State and District officials; ii) Developing curricula and training modules and partner with State Level Technical Institutes for further trainings to micro enterprises and groups; iii) Training of trainers; iv) Development of online modules for training; v) Preparation of standard Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) for typical products for micro units; vi) Development of shelf of technology/ machines for up -gradation of typical micro units; vii) Partnership with other research and training institutions for the above activities; viii) Strengthening State Level Technical Institutions

Additionally, credit linked grant is being provided to groups @35% fo r capital investment, credit linked grant for common infrastructure @ 35%. These grants would be transferred to the lending bank after sanction of the loan by the bank. 13.2 At the national level, a Nodal bank would be appointed for disbursement of subsidy to the banks and liaison with the banks. 13.3 The bank sanctioning the loan would open a mirror account in the name of the beneficiary. The lending bank would report the fact of sanction of loan to the Nodal Bank at the national level. After receipt of this inf ormation, Central and State Government should respectively transfer 60% and 40% of its share of grant to the Nodal Bank. The Nodal Bank would transfer 60% of the Central share of the grant and 40% of the State share of the grant together to the concerned l ending Bank branch. That Bank branch should place this amount in the mirror -bank account of the beneficiary. The lending bank should disburse sanction loan amount in accordance with normal banking practice to the beneficiary/supplier. 13.4 If after a period of three years from the disbursement of last tranche of the loan, the beneficiary account is still

title: PMFME Scheme Guidelines
text: place this amount in the mirror -bank account of the beneficiary. The lending bank should disburse sanction loan amount in accordance with normal banking practice to the beneficiary/supplier. 13.4 If after a period of three years from the disbursement of last tranche of the loan, the beneficiary account is still standard, and the unit is operational, this grant amount would be adjusted in the bank account of the beneficiary. If the account becomes NPA prior to three years from the date of disbursement of the loan, the grant amount would be adjusted by the Bank towards repayment by the beneficiary. If the grant amount is adjusted after three years against the loan amount in case of standard account, no interest would be payable by the borrower on the portion of the loan disbursed by the Bank equal to the grant amount from the date of receipt of the grant amount by the lending bank. 13.5 Benefit of credit guarantee coverage for loans offered under this Scheme should be provided to the borrower under the Credit Guarantee Trust for Micro & Small Enterprises through the National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company under their usual terms & conditions. title: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS) Guidelines
text: Ministry of Commerce and Industry Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade Page 1 of 14 Guidelines for Startup India Seed Fund Scheme Guidelines for Startup India Seed Fund Scheme 1. Introduction Easy availability of capital is essential for entrepreneurs at the early stages of growth of an enterprise. Funding from angel investors and venture capital firms becomes available to startups only after the proof of concept has been provided. Similarly, banks provide loans only to asset -backed applicants. It is essential to provide seed funding to startups with an innovativ e idea to conduct proof of concept trials. Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS) aims to provide financial assistance to startups for proof of concept, prototype development, product trials, market entry and commercialization. This would enable these star tups to graduate to a level where they will be able to raise investments from angel investors or venture capitalists, or seek loans from commercial banks or financial institutions. The Seed Fund will be disbursed to eligible startups through eligible incu bators across India. 2. The Requirement The Indian startup ecosystem suffers from capital inadequacy in the seed and ‘Proof of Concept’ development stage. The capital required at this stage often presents a make or break situation for startups with good busi ness ideas. Many innovative business ideas fail to take off due to the absence of this critical capital required at an early stage for proof of concept, prototype development, product trials, market entry and commercialization. Seed Fund offered to such pr omising cases can have a multiplier effect in validation of business ideas of many startups, leading to employment generation.

Eligibility Criteria: 3.1 Eligibility Criteria for Startups The eligibility criteria for a startup to apply under the Startup India Seed Fund Scheme shall be as follows: 1. A startup, recognized by DPIIT, incorporated not more than 2 years ago at the time of application 2. Startup must have a business idea to develop a product or a service with market fit, viable commercialization, and scope of scaling 3. Startup should be using technology in its core product or service, or business model, or distribution model, or methodology to solve the problem being targeted 4. Preference would be given to startups creating innovative solutions in sectors such as social impact, waste management, water management, financial inclusion, education, agriculture, food processing, biotechnology, healthcare, energy, mobility, defence, space, railways, oil and gas, textiles, etc. 5. Startup should not have received more than Rs 10 lakh of monetary support under any other Central or State Government scheme. This does not include prize money from competitions and grand challenges, subsidized working space, founder monthly allowance, access to labs, or access to prototyping facility 6. Shareholding by Indian promoters in the startup should be at least 51% at the time of application to incubator for the scheme, as per Companies Act, 2013 and SEBI (ICDR) Regulations, 2018 7. Any startup will not receive seed support more than on ce each as per provisions of para 8.1 (i) and 8.1 (ii) respectively

Incubator must be a legal entity: a) A society registered under the Societies Registration Act 1860, or b) A Trust registered under the Indian Trusts Act 1882, or c) A Private Limited company registered under the Companies Act 1956 or the Companies Act 2013, or d) A statutory body created through an Act of legislature 2. Incubator should be operational for at least two years on the date of application to the scheme 3. Incubator must have facilities to seat at least 25 individuals 4. Incubator must have at least 5 startups undergoing incubation physically on the date of application 5. Incubator must have a full -time Chief Executive Officer, experienced in business development and entrepreneurship, supported by a capable team responsible for mentoring startups in testing and validating ideas, as well as in finance, legal and human resources functions 6. Incubator should not be disbursing seed fund to incubatees using funding from any third-party private entity 7. Incubator must have been assisted by Central/State Government(s) 8. In case the incubator has not been assisted by C entral or State Government(s): a) Incubator must be operational for at least three years b) Must have at least 10 separate startups undergoing incubation in the incubator physically on the date of application c) Must present audited annual reports for the last 2 years 9. text: PLAYBOOK OF GOVERNMENT SCHEMES AND INITIATIVES FOR STARTUPS Page 32 of 107 Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS) Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) 📌 WHAT IS THIS? The Startup India Seed Fund Scheme helps new startups get early funding so they can turn ideas into real products and grow, filling the gap when they typically struggle to find initial investment. 🎯 OBJECTIVES Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS) aims to provide financial assistance to startups for proof of concept, prototype development, product trials, market entry and commercialisation. Through this funding support, startups graduate to a level where they will be able to raise investments from angel investors or venture capitalists or seek loans from commercial banks or financial institutions ✅ WHO CAN APPLY? • DPIIT recognised startups. • Incorporated not more than 2 years ago at the time of application. • Startup must have a business idea to develop a product or a service with market fit, viable commercialisation, and scope of scaling. Startup should be using technology in its core product or service, or business model. • Startup should not have received more than ₹10 lakh of monetary support under any other Central or State Government scheme 💰 WHAT DO YOU GET? • Up to ₹20 lakh as grant for validation of Proof of Concept, or prototype development, or product trials. • Up to ₹50 lakh of investment for market entry, commercialisation, or scaling up through convertible debentures or debt or debt -linked instruments 🚀 HOW TO APPLY Visit https://seedfund.startupindia.gov.in/ to apply. Last date for startups to apply under SISFS was 31 May 2026. Disbursals are ongoing. 🔗 KEY LINKS • Website: https://seedfund.startupindia.gov.in/ • Guidelines: https://www.startupindia.gov.in/content/dam/invest- india/Templates/public/Guidelines%20for%20Startup%20India%20Seed %20Fund%20Scheme.pdf 💡 BEST SUITED FOR Seed / Early-Stage

text: PLAYBOOK OF GOVERNMENT SCHEMES AND INITIATIVES FOR STARTUPS Page 33 of 107 Fund of Funds for Startups (FFS) Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) 📌 WHAT IS THIS? The Fund of Funds for Startups (FFS) provides capital to venture funds so they can invest in startups, helping increase the availability of funding and support the growth of India’s startup ecosystem. 🎯 OBJECTIVES The Government has established FFS to catalyze venture capital investments. It is operationalized by Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI), which provides capital to SEBI -registered Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) who in turn invest in startups through equity and equity-linked instruments. ✅ WHO CAN APPLY? • SEBI-registered AIFs can apply for capital under the Scheme. • The funding is provided to DPIIT recognised startups by selected AIFs. 💰 WHAT DO YOU GET? The Scheme has a corpus of ₹10,000 crore, which is aimed to be provided to startup through AIFs. The AIFs supported under the Scheme are to invest at least twice the contribution out of FFS in startups across stages 🚀 HOW TO APPLY • The application process for AIFs has been digitali sed and a detailed application can be submitted by the AIFs on SIDBI’s Fund Application Portal (https://vcfapplication.sidbi.in/login). The AIF applications undergo an eligibility screening and screening based on preliminary questionnaire. • Eligible startups can approach selected AIFs for investments. 🔗 KEY LINKS • Website: https://www.sidbivcf.in/en/funds/ffs • Operational guidelines: https://www.dpiit.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/07/ccffbf768a90e8445ba78f 82d4c42bec.pdf 💡 BEST SUITED FOR Scaling

Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0 supports startups by channeling government capital into venture funds to boost investment in emerging businesses, aiming to fuel innovation in priority sectors. 🎯 OBJECTIVES • The Government operationalized the Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0 (Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0 (FoF 2.0)) with a total corpus of ₹10,000 crore. Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI), Implementation Agency (IA) of the FFS 1.0, shall also be the Implementing Agency for the Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0 (FoF 2.0). • In addition, another domestic IA(s) shall also be selected to implement the proposed Scheme. The IA(s) will provide capital to SEBI -registered Category I and Category II Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) who in turn will invest in startups through equity and equity-linked instruments. • Investments under Startup India FoF 2.0 AIFs supporting priority segments including deep tech startups, early growth stage startups supported by smaller AIFs, technology -driven and innovative manufacturing startups, and sector or stage agnostic startups. ✅ WHO CAN APPLY? • SEBI-registered AIFs can apply for capital under the Scheme. • The funding is provided to DPIIT recognised startups by selected AIFs. 💰 WHAT DO YOU GET? The Scheme has a corpus of ₹10,000 crore, which is aimed to be provided to startup through AIFs. AIFs supported under the Scheme are required to invest in startups across stages, adhering to the minimum investment multiplier for various segments as defined in the Operational Guidelines. 🚀 HOW TO APPLY • The application process for AIFs has been digitali sed and a detailed application can be submitted by the AIFs on SIDBI’s Fund

text: PLAYBOOK OF GOVERNMENT SCHEMES AND INITIATIVES FOR STARTUPS Page 35 of 107 Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups (CGSS) Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) 📌 WHAT IS THIS? The Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups (CGSS) helps startups access loans by assuring lenders that the government will cover part of the risk, making it easier for young businesses to get funding without collateral. 🎯 OBJECTIVES • Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups (CGSS) aims at providing credit guarantee up to a specified limit against loans extended by Member Institutions (MIs) to finance eligible borrowers viz. entities recognised as ‘startups’ by DPIIT. CGSS is operated by the National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company (NCGTC) Limited. ✅ WHO CAN APPLY? • Eligible (i) Scheduled Commercial Banks and Financial Institutions; (ii) RBI registered Non -Banking Finance Companies (NBFCs) and (iii) Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) registered Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) can become member instituti ons (MIs) subject to requirements. • Eligible borrowers are DPIIT recognised startups. 💰 WHAT DO YOU GET? Maximum guarantee of ₹20 crore or actual outstanding credit amount, whichever is less. For both transaction-based and umbrella-based cover. 🚀 HOW TO APPLY • Visit the website for details: https://www.ncgtc.in/en/product- details/CGSS/Credit-Guarantee%20Scheme%20for%20Start- ups%20(CGSS) • For application through the Jan Samarth portal: https://www.jansamarth.in/business-loan-startup-scheme. 🔗 KEY LINKS • Scheme information and application instructions: https://www.ncgtc.in/en/product-details/CGSS/Credit- Guarantee%20Scheme%20for%20Start-ups%20(CGSS) 💡 BEST SUITED FOR Credit Support

text: PLAYBOOK OF GOVERNMENT SCHEMES AND INITIATIVES FOR STARTUPS Page 36 of 107 Scheme for Facilitating Startups Intellectual Property Protection (SIPP) Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) 📌 WHAT IS THIS? The Scheme for Facilitating Startups Intellectual Property Protection (SIPP) helps startups protect their ideas by providing support and cost relief for filing patents, trademarks, and designs, encouraging innovation and safeguarding ownership. 🎯 OBJECTIVES • To protect and promote Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) of Startups and to encourage innovation and creativity among them, a Scheme for facilitating Start -Ups Intellectual Property Protection (SIPP) has been launched. • It facilitates startups in filing and processing of their patent, design or trademark application through the assistance of IP Facilitators, whose fee was borne by the Office of the Controller General of Patents Designs and Trademarks, Department for Promo tion of Industry and Internal Trade, Government of India. ✅ WHO CAN APPLY? • DPIIT recognised startups. • Applicants must self -declare that they have not availed funds under any other government scheme for paying facilitator/patent agent/trademark agent fees for the same IP application. 💰 WHAT DO YOU GET? • Support for filing and processing patent, trademark and design applications. • Professional fees of facilitators are paid/reimbursed by the office of CGPDTM; startups generally bear only statutory government fees. • End-to-end assistance including advisory, drafting, filing, responses to examination reports, hearings, opposition handling and final disposal of IP applications. 🚀 HOW TO APPLY • Visit IP India SIPP Page / Facilitator Details: https://ipindia.gov.in/page- content/startups-intellectual-property-protection-sipp 🔗 KEY LINKS • DPIIT SIPP Scheme Page: https://www.dpiit.gov.in/offerings/schemes- and-services/details/sipp-gTM1UDNtQWa • IP India SIPP Page / Facilitator Details: https://ipindia.gov.in/page- content/startups-intellectual-property-protection-sipp 💡 BEST SUITED FOR Any Stage

text: PLAYBOOK OF GOVERNMENT SCHEMES AND INITIATIVES FOR STARTUPS Page 37 of 107 GeM Startup Runway Department of Commerce 📌 WHAT IS THIS? The GeM Startup Runway enables startups to showcase and sell their innovative products directly to government buyers, helping them access public procurement opportunities and grow their business. 🎯 OBJECTIVES • GeM Startup Runway helps startups sell innovative products and services directly to government buyers through the Government e -Marketplace (GeM) by promoting solutions that are unique in concept, design, process, or functionality and improve startup participation in public procurement. ✅ WHO CAN APPLY? • DPIIT-recognised startups registered as sellers/service providers on GeM. • Startups with products/services in existing GeM categories or in dedicated startup sectors such as AI, robotics, agritech, cleantech, cybersecurity, edtech, health tech, water tech, assistive tech, etc. • Other innovative entities. 💰 WHAT DO YOU GET? • Access to a large base of government buyers across ministries, departments, PSUs and other public entities. • Exemption/relaxation from requirements such as prior turnover, prior experience, and Earnest Money Deposit (EMD). • Dedicated marketplace visibility for startups and innovative products. • Ability to list innovative products even when standard categories may not exist. 🚀 HOW TO APPLY • Visit GeM Startup Runway: https://gem.gov.in/Startup_Runway 🔗 KEY LINKS • GeM Startup Runway: https://gem.gov.in/Startup_Runway • Startup India – Public Procurement / GeM: https://www.startupindia.gov.in/content/sih/en/public_procurement.html 💡 BEST SUITED FOR Any Stage

text: PLAYBOOK OF GOVERNMENT SCHEMES AND INITIATIVES FOR STARTUPS Page 38 of 107 NIDHI – Seed Support Program (SSP) Department of Science & Technology (DST) 📌 WHAT IS THIS? The NIDHI – Seed Support Program (SSP) provides early-stage funding and support to innovators to help them develop and validate their ideas, encouraging the creation of viable startups. 🎯 OBJECTIVES • NIDHI-Seed Support Program (SSP) aims to provide seed support to deserving incubatee startups, through NIDHI Science & Technology Entrepreneurs Parks (STEPs) and NIDHI Technology Business Incubators (TBIs). ✅ WHO CAN APPLY? • Incubatee should be a DPIIT recognised startup with minimum of three months of residency at the STEPs/TBIs. The shareholding by Indian promoters in the incubatee startup should be at least 51%. 💰 WHAT DO YOU GET? • Under the program, the startups are supported primarily for product development, testing and trials, test marketing, mentoring, professional consultancy (to attract professors/experts from institutions to work with startups.), IPR issues and any other area as deemed necessary and recommended by the Seed Support Management Committee of STEP/TBIs. 🚀 HOW TO APPLY • Applications details are released on the website https://nidhi.dst.gov.in/nidhissp/ 🔗 KEY LINKS • Website: https://nidhi.dst.gov.in/nidhissp/ 💡 BEST SUITED FOR Seed / Post-Incubation

text: PLAYBOOK OF GOVERNMENT SCHEMES AND INITIATIVES FOR STARTUPS Page 39 of 107 NIDHI – Promotion and Acceleration of Young and Aspiring Technology Entrepreneurs (PRAYAS) 2.0 Department of Science & Technology (DST) 📌 WHAT IS THIS? The NIDHI PRAYAS 2.0 scheme provides early -stage funding and prototyping support to young innovators, helping them turn their technology ideas into working products and viable startups. 🎯 OBJECTIVES • The scheme aims to bridge the gap funding in the very early -stage idea/ proof of concept. Building on the outcomes of NIDHI PRAYAS 1.0, the programme has evolved into NIDHI PRAYAS 2.0, with enhanced support for both technology -based and deep -tech innovatio ns. It is a pre - incubation initiative that is implemented through incubators known as the PRAYAS Centres (PCs) and Advance PRAYAS Centres (APCs) (specialized centres to support DeepTech innovations). ✅ WHO CAN APPLY? • A DPIIT recognised startup or an individual innovator are eligible to apply under the program. • In case of a recognised startup, it has to be incorporated in India, not more than 5 years of existence and its annual turnover for any financial year should not have exceeded ₹1 crore. 💰 WHAT DO YOU GET? • Level 1 – PCs: Each innovator/startup supported by a Level 1 Centre PC may receive up to ₹20 Lakhs grant for prototyping. DST provides up to ₹2 crore per annum to each PC. • Level 2 – APCs: Provides prototyping grants of up to ₹40 lakh per innovator/ startup. DST provides up to ₹4 crore per annum to each APC. 🚀 HOW TO APPLY • Applicant incubators can submit the proposal online in the prescribed proforma, at the NIDHI PRAYAS PMU Portal https://nidhi-prayas.org/ or on https://nidhi.dst.gov.in/schemes- programmes/nidhiprayas/ 🔗 KEY LINKS • Website: https://nidhi-prayas.org/ • Operational Guidelines: https://nidhi-prayas.org/documents/dst-nidhi- prayas-2.0-program-guidelines-2026.pdf 💡 BEST

text: PLAYBOOK OF GOVERNMENT SCHEMES AND INITIATIVES FOR STARTUPS Page 40 of 107 Research, Development & Innovation (RDI) Scheme Department of Science & Technology (DST) 📌 WHAT IS THIS? The Research, Development & Innovation (RDI) Scheme provides funding and support to help organizations create and improve new technologies or ideas so they can boost innovation, economic growth, and global competitiveness. 🎯 OBJECTIVES • DST has launched the Research, Development, and Innovation (RDI) Scheme, approved by the Cabinet on 1st July 2025, with a total outlay of ₹1 lakh crore. • The initiative aims to catalyze private sector participation in high -impact R&D and strengthen India’s capabilities in strategic technologies and promote technological self -reliance, aligning with the nation’s long -term innovation and Atmanirbhar Bharat vision. ✅ WHO CAN APPLY? • The RDI Fund is provided to Second Level Fund Managers (SLFM) which include Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs), Development Finance Institutions (DFIs), Non -Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs), and Focused Research Organisations (FROs). • The SLFM then provides funds to private companies including DPIIT recognised startups advancing RDI-intensive technologies. 💰 WHAT DO YOU GET? • Loan – Debt funding (via loan or optionally convertible debt) from the SLFM, calculated as 50% of the project cost. • Equity – Funding via equity or equity linked instruments from the SLFM, calculated as 50% of the value of each funding round. 🚀 HOW TO APPLY • Visit - https://rdifund.anrf.gov.in/images/pdf/RDIF-%20AIF_and_FOF.pdf • Startups can apply directly through the SLFMs, for instance the Technology Development Board (TDB) (https://www.e- techcom.tdb.gov.in/rdif-registration.php 🔗 KEY LINKS • Website: https://rdifund.anrf.gov.in/ • Operational Guidelines: https://rdifund.anrf.gov.in/images/pdf/2026_IG.pdf 💡 BEST SUITED FOR Deep-Tech Scaling

text: PLAYBOOK OF GOVERNMENT SCHEMES AND INITIATIVES FOR STARTUPS Page 41 of 107 National Quantum Mission (NQM) Department of Science & Technology (DST) 📌 WHAT IS THIS? The National Quantum Mission (NQM) supports research and development of advanced quantum technologies (like quantum computing and secure communication) so India can build cutting -edge capabilities and stay competitive in future tech. 🎯 OBJECTIVES • The National Quantum Mission (NQM) aims to seed, nurture and scale up scientific and industrial R&D and create a vibrant & innovative ecosystem in Quantum Technology (QT) in the country. • As part of the mission, four Thematic Hubs (T -Hubs) will be established as Section-8 Companies, not -for-profit entities, within premier academic institutions and national research and development labs. These T -Hubs will specialize in four distinct technolo gy verticals: Quantum Computing, Quantum Communication, Quantum Sensing & Metrology, and Quantum Materials & Devices. ✅ WHO CAN APPLY? • Academic institutions, R&D labs, and consortia working in quantum computing, communication, sensing/metrology, and materials/devices. • Startups working in quantum technology, preferably DPIIT-registered and Indian-owned/controlled as per startup support guidelines. • For teaching lab support, eligible institutions include Government - funded/aided technical institutions/universities and eligible AICTE/UGC - recognised institutions meeting quality benchmarks. 💰 WHAT DO YOU GET? • Funding and institutional support for quantum R&D, prototypes, product development, and commercialisation through NQM T-Hubs. • Startup support can include seed/prototype funding and scale-up support routed through T-Hubs/TIHs. • Creation of skilled manpower, research infrastructure, and industry - academia collaboration in quantum technologies. 🚀 HOW TO APPLY • Startups apply through online calls/challenges; applications are evaluated on need, feasibility, impact, novelty, team strength, and fund -utilization plan. • Other applicants apply through DST/NQM calls or the relevant Thematic Hub (T-Hub) based on the focus area 🔗 KEY LINKS • National Quantum Mission: https://www.psa.gov.in/mission/national-

The PRISM scheme provides funding and support to individual innovators, startups, and small businesses so they can turn new ideas into useful products and grow their businesses. 🎯 OBJECTIVES • PRISM (Promoting Innovations in Individuals, Start -ups and MSMEs) Scheme supports individual innovators with financial assistance that helps them build prototypes, develop technologies, and move toward patenting & commercialisation. • DSIR has established a robust mechanism to implement this scheme across the country through TePP Outreach cum Cluster Innovation Centres (TOCICs) in Universities and National research laboratories and PRISM Advisory and Screening Committee PASC at Delhi to receive and evaluate the proposals from innovators for funding. ✅ WHO CAN APPLY? • Public funded institutions or organizations viz. Autonomous Organizations or Society registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860 or Indian Trusts Act, 1882 engaged in promotion of innovation. Any Indian citizen having an innovative idea and wish to translate their idea into working prototypes/models/processes. 💰 WHAT DO YOU GET? text: PLAYBOOK OF GOVERNMENT SCHEMES AND INITIATIVES FOR STARTUPS Page 43 of 107 Biotechnology Ignition Grant Scheme (BIG) Department of Biotechnology / Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC) 📌 WHAT IS THIS? The Biotechnology Ignition Grant (BIG) Scheme provides early-stage funding and support to biotech innovators and startups so they can turn promising scientific ideas into viable products and businesses. 🎯 OBJECTIVES • Biotechnology Ignition Grant (BIG) is a flagship programme of BIRAC, which provides support to young startups and entrepreneurial individuals. BIG is the largest early-stage biotech funding programme in India. ✅ WHO CAN APPLY? • Individual Entrepreneurs and startups • The applicant must be incubated in an incubator (may/may not be supported by BIRAC). 💰 WHAT DO YOU GET? • Grant-in-aid of up to ₹50 lakh provided to startup for a period of up to 18 months. • During the BIG tenure, BIRAC extends several networking opportunities to connect with experts, mentors, industry, investors, peer to peer learning, specialized trainings & workshops, exposure to various platforms on merit basis 🚀 HOW TO APPLY • BIRAC issues a national call inviting applications under BIG at least twice a year (typically on 1st of January & 1st of July). The Call for Proposals is typically open for a period of 30-45 days. Application for BIG needs to be submitted online only through BIRAC website www.birac.nic.in 🔗 KEY LINKS • Detailed guidelines: https://birac.nic.in/webcontent/1761936564_big_new_guidelines_nov_20 25.pdf • FAQs: https://birac.nic.in/big.php 💡 BEST SUITED FOR Ideation to PoC

The Biotechnology Innovation Fund – Accelerating Entrepreneurs (AcE) provides financial support to biotech startups so they can develop and scale innovative solutions faster and bring them to market. 🎯 OBJECTIVES • The AcE Fund is a ‘fund of funds’ that aims to partner with fund managers (AcE Fund Partners) and invest in SEBI -registered AIFs (Daughter Funds). AcE Daughter Funds commit investment of 2x BIRAC’s contribution into biotech startups. ✅ WHO CAN APPLY? • AcE Fund invests and partners with SEBI -registered Category I and II AIFs in biotech sector. • Startups and SMEs in subsectors such as Healthcare, Life Sciences, Pharma, Biopharma, Med-tech, Diagnostics, Industrial-Biotech, Agri-tech, Bio-IT/Services and allied areas. 💰 WHAT DO YOU GET? • The AcE Fund shall make a maximum capital commitment of up to ₹30 crore or up to 30% of the total aggregate capital commitment amount (i.e. fund corpus) in each Daughter Fund. • Ticket size of up to ₹7 crore, with provision of additional follow-on funding up to ₹3.5 crore is provided to an eligible startup. 🚀 HOW TO APPLY • Apply on: https://birac.nic.in/aceFund.php 🔗 KEY LINKS • Guidelines: https://birac.nic.in/webcontent/ace_fund_guidelines.pdf ; https://birac.nic.in/webcontent/fund_of_funds_AcE_fund.pdf • FAQs: https://birac.nic.in/webcontent/1680262332_AcE_FAQ_revised.pdf 💡 BEST SUITED FOR Scaling

The BIRAC Incubator SEED Fund (SEED) provides early -stage funding through incubators to biotech startups so they can develop their ideas into viable products and launch successful businesses. 🎯 OBJECTIVES • BIRAC Sustainable Entrepreneurship and Enterprise Development Fund (“SEED Fund”) primarily addresses the financial support requirements of technology startups in their initial phase of operations. Funding is disbursed to startups under this program through the incubators. The funding support aims to enhance startups’ ability to raise investments from Angel/Venture capitalist or to seek loans from commercial banks /financial institutions. ✅ WHO CAN APPLY? • Biotech/Med-Tech/Life Sciences startups. 💰 WHAT DO YOU GET? • Seed funding as equity and equity linked instruments up to ₹30 lakh per startup. 🚀 HOW TO APPLY • Refer to the BIRAC Incubator SEED Fund Scheme website for more information of the incubators associated with the program: https://www.birac.nic.in/seedFundNew.php 🔗 KEY LINKS • Website: https://www.birac.nic.in/seedFundNew.php • Operational Guidelines: https://www.birac.nic.in/webcontent/1616486925_seed_fund_Guidelines. pdf 💡 BEST SUITED FOR Seed

The LEAP Fund supports entrepreneurs in creating affordable, innovative products so more people can access useful technologies while encouraging business growth. 🎯 OBJECTIVES • LEAP Fund assists potential biotech startups in piloting & commercialising their products & technologies enabling them to raise venture capital investment. ✅ WHO CAN APPLY? • Startups in Biotech/med-tech/life science sectors. 💰 WHAT DO YOU GET? • Funding support of more than ₹30 lakh and up to ₹1 crore per startup. Startup eligible and suitable for up to the threshold of ₹30 lakh investment support will be considered under SEED fund and not the LEAP fund. • BioNEST Bioincubators (LEAP fund partners) will be given up to ₹5 crore fund/ partner for investing in potential startup against equity and equity linked instruments. 🚀 HOW TO APPLY • Apply on: https://birac.nic.in/leapFundNew.php 🔗 KEY LINKS • Operational Guidelines: https://birac.nic.in/webcontent/1616486900_leap_fund_guidelines.pdf 💡 BEST SUITED FOR Commercialisation

text: PLAYBOOK OF GOVERNMENT SCHEMES AND INITIATIVES FOR STARTUPS Page 47 of 107 SPARSH – Social Innovation Programme for Products Affordable & Relevant to Social Health Department of Biotechnology (DBT) / BIRAC 📌 WHAT IS THIS? The SPARSH programme supports innovators in developing affordable health-related solutions so that essential healthcare products can reach and benefit underserved communities. 🎯 OBJECTIVES • SPARSH, the social innovation initiative designed biotechnological interventions to address critical societal issues. • SPARSH revolves around nurturing "Social Innovators" within the biotech domain, equipped to identify community needs and gaps, and formulate innovative product developments or services to bridge these disparities. ✅ WHO CAN APPLY? • There are two components under the initiative – (i) Affordable Product Development and (ii) Social Innovation Immersion Program (SIIP). Startups and entrepreneurs are eligible for Category A under Component I. Specific eligibility criteria include the following: • Biotechnology Indian startups (less than 3 years old) • Limited Liability Partnership (LLP) – less than 3 years old • Indian academic scientists, researchers etc. 💰 WHAT DO YOU GET? • Grant-in-aid assistance up to ₹50 lakh for a period of up to 18 months. 🚀 HOW TO APPLY • The call for Letter of Intent (LoI) is announced twice a year on a thematic area with high societal impact • The LoI is to be submitted online on the BIRAC website: https://www.birac.nic.in/ 🔗 KEY LINKS • Website: https://www.birac.nic.in/ • Operational Guidelines: https://birac.nic.in/webcontent/Sparsh_Guidelines_Ver4.pdf 💡 BEST SUITED FOR Ideation to Validation

text: PLAYBOOK OF GOVERNMENT SCHEMES AND INITIATIVES FOR STARTUPS Page 48 of 107 AgriSURE – Agri Fund for Startups & Rural Enterprises Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare 📌 WHAT IS THIS? The AgriSURE Fund supports agri-startups and rural enterprises with funding and resources so they can develop innovative farming and rural solutions, improving livelihoods and strengthening the agricultural sector. 🎯 OBJECTIVES • With a focus on technology -driven, high -risk, high -impact ventures, AgriSURE is designed to fuel growth and foster innovation in the agricultural and rural startup ecosystem. A blended capital fund of ₹750 crore with SEBI Registered Category II, Alternative Investment Fund (AIF), contributions from the Government of India is ₹250 crore, NABARD is ₹250 crore, and ₹250 crore is being mobilized from banks, insurance companies, and private investors. • Aims to support innovative, technology -driven, high -impact startups in agriculture and allied sectors, improve the farm produce value chain, including support for FPOs/FPCs, farm mechanisation, IT-based solutions and rural enterprises, attract more investm ent into the agri and rural startup ecosystem through AIFs and direct investments, and create employment opportunities and encourage youth entrepreneurship in agriculture. ✅ WHO CAN APPLY? • Startups working in agriculture and rural development sectors. • SEBI-registered Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs), sector -specific, sector-agnostic and debt AIFs that invest in agri/rural startups 💰 WHAT DO YOU GET? • Investment through two routes: Fund of Funds Scheme with ₹450 crore corpus and Direct Scheme with ₹300 crore corpus. • Supports around 85 startups, with ticket size up to ₹25 crore, subject to investment merit and fund guidelines. • Provides grant -in-aid, incubation and mentoring support to eligible agri startups. 🚀 HOW TO APPLY • Eligible startups or AIFs can approach NABVENTURES . https://nabventures.in/agrisure.aspx 🔗 KEY LINKS • NABARD AgriSURE page: https://www.nabard.org/agrisure.aspx • NABVENTURES AgriSURE

text: PLAYBOOK OF GOVERNMENT SCHEMES AND INITIATIVES FOR STARTUPS Page 50 of 107 SAMRIDH – Startup Accelerators of MeitY for Product Innovation, Development & Growth Ministry of Electronics & Information Technology (MeitY) 📌 WHAT IS THIS? SAMRIDH is a government program that supports startups by funding and accelerating innovative tech products so they can grow faster and succeed in the market. 🎯 OBJECTIVES • The SAMRIDH scheme supports existing and upcoming Accelerators to select and accelerate potential IT-based startups to scale. • The programme focuses on accelerating the startup by providing customer connect, investor connect, and internationalisation connect services. • The Scheme supports selected Accelerators for extending Accelerator services to startup and provide funding. ✅ WHO CAN APPLY? • Accelerators – registered as Section 8 company under Companies Act 2013 or as Society under Societies Registration Act (not-for-profit). • IT-based startups. 💰 WHAT DO YOU GET? • To startups: An investment of up to ₹40 lakh to the beneficiary startup (with an average of ₹30 lakh per startup per cohort). An equal matching private investment by the accelerator / investor of up to ₹40 lakh is disbursed to startups based on their current valuation and growth stage. • To Accelerators: Accelerators develop customized acceleration programs to fit the needs of each startup in the cohort and provide services ranging from customer connect, investor connect, capacity enhancement, product enhancement etc. for which they are provided a budget of ₹2 lakh per startup to a maximum of ₹20 lakh per cohort. 🚀 HOW TO APPLY • Startups to refer to the MeitY Startup Hub (MSH) to access the list of incubators and accelerators in India benefitting from the SAMRIDH scheme and gauge the accelerators most suitable to their needs. 🔗 KEY LINKS • Website: https://msh.meity.gov.in/schemes/samridh • Operational Guidelines: https://msh.meity.gov.in/assets/Scheme- Report.pdf 💡 BEST SUITED

text: PLAYBOOK OF GOVERNMENT SCHEMES AND INITIATIVES FOR STARTUPS Page 51 of 107 GENESIS – Gen-Next Support for Innovative Startups Ministry of Electronics & Information Technology (MeitY) 📌 WHAT IS THIS? GENESIS is a government scheme that helps early-stage startups turn innovative ideas into viable businesses by providing funding, support, and guidance so new ventures can grow and create economic value. 🎯 OBJECTIVES • The Gen -Next Support for Innovative Startups (GENESIS) supports eligible Implementing Agencies (IAs) to provide funding, mentor access, and access to innovation infrastructure and ecosystem to technology startups in Tier-II and Tier-III cities in India. ✅ WHO CAN APPLY? • Entities registered under Section 8, Incubators, Accelerators, Educational Institutes recognised by UGC/AICTE/Formed under Central/State Act and other startups ecosystem entities that are engaged in supporting startups. 💰 WHAT DO YOU GET? • Recurring financial support will be offered to approximately 50 IAs for the duration of the scheme. • Investment and pilot funding support to startups ranging from ₹10 lakh (for early-stage startups), to up to ₹1 crore (deep-tech startups). • Capacity building initiatives for the startup ecosystem in Tier II and III cities. 🚀 HOW TO APPLY • Applications are accepted throughout the year. • Interested applicants may submit their applications online via https://msh.meity.gov.in/schemes/genesis 🔗 KEY LINKS • https://www.meity.gov.in/static/uploads/2024/02/GENESIS_Admin_Appr oval-1.pdf • https://www.meity.gov.in/static/uploads/2024/02/Brochure_GENESIS.pd f 💡 BEST SUITED FOR Ideation to Scaling

text: PLAYBOOK OF GOVERNMENT SCHEMES AND INITIATIVES FOR STARTUPS Page 52 of 107 STPI – Next Generation Incubation Scheme (NGIS) Ministry of Electronics & Information Technology (MeitY) / STPI 📌 WHAT IS THIS? NGIS is a government scheme that helps nurture early-stage tech startups by providing incubation support, funding, and mentorship so they can develop strong, scalable business ideas. 🎯 OBJECTIVES • It is a startup incubation scheme by Software Technology Parks of India (STPI) under MeitY, aimed at strengthening India’s software product startup ecosystem, especially in Tier -II/III cities. It aims to handhold 300 tech startups across 12 STPI incubation locations in Tier-II/III cities. ✅ WHO CAN APPLY? • Indian startups working on software product development / technology - based solutions. • DPIIT-recognised startups are encouraged; individuals, academicians, researchers, entrepreneurs, LLPs, and partnership firms may also participate but may need to register as a private limited company if selected. 💰 WHAT DO YOU GET? • Seed / risk funding up to ₹25 lakh for promising startups. • Access to state-of-the-art incubation infrastructure, labs, equipment, and testing facilities. • Mentoring, startup-connect, industry networking, marketing support, and product lifecycle guidance. • Internship / challenge grants for selected startups. 🚀 HOW TO APPLY • Applicants submit proposals online through the STPI/NGIS application portal during open calls. 🔗 KEY LINKS • STPI Startup Portal: https://startup.stpi.in/ 💡 BEST SUITED FOR Ideation to Scaling

text: PLAYBOOK OF GOVERNMENT SCHEMES AND INITIATIVES FOR STARTUPS Page 53 of 107 Chips to Startup (C2S) Programme Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) 📌 WHAT IS THIS? The program is to build India’s semiconductor/chip -design ecosystem by training skilled manpower and supporting chip development. 🎯 OBJECTIVES • It aims to train specialised professionals in VLSI and Embedded System Design over 5 years, promote design and development of ASICs, SoCs, FPGAs, reusable IP cores, and prototypes, and create a strong fabless chip-design startup ecosystem in India and supp ort indigenous semiconductor innovation. ✅ WHO CAN APPLY? • Academic institutions and R&D organisations across India, including IITs, NITs, IIITs, government/private colleges, and R&D bodies. • Startups and MSMEs can participate through academia -industry collaborative projects, grand challenges, hackathons, or RFPs for System/SoC/IP Core development. 💰 WHAT DO YOU GET? • Financial and technical support for chip -design projects under approved categories. • Access to chip -design ecosystem support such as EDA tools, IP repository, fabrication/MPW support, prototyping, and mentoring. • Support for manpower training, R&D, hardware IP design, system design, prototype development, and deployment. 🚀 HOW TO APPLY • Applicants submit project proposals online through the C2S portal in the prescribed MeitY provided format. 🔗 KEY LINKS • C2S Official Portal: https://www.c2s.gov.in/ • About C2S: https://www.c2s.gov.in/about_c2s.jsp 💡 BEST SUITED FOR R&D to Prototype

text: PLAYBOOK OF GOVERNMENT SCHEMES AND INITIATIVES FOR STARTUPS Page 54 of 107 Innovations for Defence Excellence (iDEX) Ministry of Defence / Defence Innovation Organisation (DIO) 📌 WHAT IS THIS? iDEX is a government initiative that supports startups and innovators in building defence solutions so the military can access advanced, homegrown technologies and reduce reliance on imports. 🎯 OBJECTIVES • Innovations for Defence Excellence (iDEX) is the operational framework of the Defence Innovation Organization (DIO), a special purpose vehicle under the aegis of the Department of Defence Production, Ministry of Defence. • The iDEX framework was launched in 2018 to support the attainment of self-reliance in the fields of defence and defence production. • iDEX partners with incubators, i.e. Partner Incubators (PIs) to facilitate mentoring and access to infrastructure/test facilities to innovators, including amongst the smaller enterprises, startups and MSMES, to foster innovation in the defense sector in an integrated manner. ✅ WHO CAN APPLY? • DPIIT recognised startups. • Any company incorporated under the Companies Act, primarily a MSME as defined under the MSME Act 2016. • Individual innovators can also apply. 💰 WHAT DO YOU GET? • Beneficiaries are provided grants/funding and other support to carry out R&D development. • Innovation activities like accelerator programs, challenges etc., are carried under the initiative, by the iDEX Partner Incubators. • Grants ranging from ₹1.5 crore to ₹10 crore awarded to startups based on the scheme/challenge applied to. 🚀 HOW TO APPLY • Visit https://idex.gov.in/challenges for more information on Challenges organized under iDEX. 🔗 KEY LINKS • Operational guidelines: https://idex.gov.in/res 💡 BEST SUITED FOR Prototype to Procurement

text: PLAYBOOK OF GOVERNMENT SCHEMES AND INITIATIVES FOR STARTUPS Page 55 of 107 Acing Development of Innovative Technologies with iDEX (ADITI) Ministry of Defence / Defence Innovation Organisation (DIO) 📌 WHAT IS THIS? ADITI is a government program that supports startups and innovators in building new defence and aerospace technologies so India can become more self‑reliant and technologically advanced. 🎯 OBJECTIVES • The ADITI Scheme aims to facilitate rapid development of strategically critical technologies which are sensitive and innovative from the defence perspective and required by the country. • Under this, relevant Challenges/Hackathons are organized for startups to seek solutions for problem statements pertaining to the earmarked technology. Winners of the ADITI challenges are incubated by Partner Incubators (PIs). ✅ WHO CAN APPLY? • DPIIT recognised startups. • Any Indian company incorporated under the Companies Act 1956/2013. • Individual innovators can also apply. 💰 WHAT DO YOU GET? • For Partner Incubators: The limit of payment amounting to ₹9 lakh per PI, based on facilitation/completion of each milestone of their associated challenge winner. • For Startups/Innovators: Quantum of Grant up to 50% of product development budget (PDB) with maximum limit of ₹25 crore, leading to a PDB around ₹50 crore or beyond. 🚀 HOW TO APPLY • Visit https://idex.gov.in/ for more information. 🔗 KEY LINKS • Website: https://idex.gov.in/ • Operational guidelines: https://idex.gov.in//uploads/page/aditi_scheeme.pdf 💡 BEST SUITED FOR Advanced Prototype

text: PLAYBOOK OF GOVERNMENT SCHEMES AND INITIATIVES FOR STARTUPS Page 56 of 107 Technology Development Fund (TDF) DRDO, Ministry of Defence 📌 WHAT IS THIS? Technology Development Fund (TDF) is a government scheme that gives funding and support to Indian companies and startups to develop defence technologies locally so the country can reduce dependence on imports and strengthen self-reliance. 🎯 OBJECTIVES • The TDF Scheme has been established to promote self -reliance in defence technology as a part of the 'Make in India' initiative. • The Scheme enlists requirements of Service Headquarters (SHQs) of upgrading products/ systems and futuristic defence technologies as Projects for which eligible stakeholders can apply through their platform. ✅ WHO CAN APPLY? • Public limited company, a private limited company, a partnership firm, a limited liability partnership, one -person company, sole proprietorship registered as per applicable Indian laws. • DPIIT recogni sed startup s that should be incubated at one of the Central/State Government assisted incubators. • At least 50% of the shares of the startup must be owned and controlled by Indian citizens. 💰 WHAT DO YOU GET? • The funding will be through provision of grants. • Project cost of up to ₹10 crore will be considered for funding, subject to a maximum funding of 90%. • Aims to provide financial assistance to startups for prototype development and trials. 🚀 HOW TO APPLY • Application process for the TDF is digitized. Applicants can register on the TDF portal - https://tdf.drdo.gov.in/ 🔗 KEY LINKS • Website: https://tdf.drdo.gov.in/ 💡 BEST SUITED FOR Prototype to Product

text: PLAYBOOK OF GOVERNMENT SCHEMES AND INITIATIVES FOR STARTUPS Page 57 of 107 IN-SPACe Seed Fund Scheme IN-SPACe, Department of Space 📌 WHAT IS THIS? IN-SPACe Seed Fund Scheme helps early-stage space startups build and test new space -tech ideas by giving them grant funding, mentoring, and support to move from concept to prototype. 🎯 OBJECTIVES • The Indian National Space Promotion and Authorization Centre (IN - SPACe) has been formed under the Department of Space (DoS) to promote, enable, authorize and supervise non -government entities to undertake space activities. ✅ WHO CAN APPLY? • DPIIT recognised early-stage startups with innovative ideas and projects that use space technology to address challenges in space sector • Startups should not have received more than ₹50 lakh of monetary support under any Central or State Government Scheme. 💰 WHAT DO YOU GET? • Funding, mentorship, training and networking opportunities. • Grant of ₹1 crore provided to selected startups on milestone-basis. 🚀 HOW TO APPLY • Announcement of opportunities made from time to time on https://www.inspace.gov.in/inspace?id=announcement_for_opportunities 🔗 KEY LINKS • Website: https://www.inspace.gov.in/inspace?id=announcement_for_opportunities • Guidelines: https://www.google.com/url?sa=t&rct=j&q=&esrc=s&source=web&cd=&c ad=rja&uact=8&ved=2ahUKEwiW5aGn3vuRAxXQUGcHHWntG8sQFno ECBsQAQ&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.inspace.gov.in%2Fsys_attachm ent.do%3Fsys_id%3D2d09969c879a755082e163d70cbb3518&usg=AO vVaw2w0pT1229-wJskQEypKV3p&opi=89978449 💡 BEST SUITED FOR Seed

text: PLAYBOOK OF GOVERNMENT SCHEMES AND INITIATIVES FOR STARTUPS Page 58 of 107 Digital Communication Innovation Square (DCIS) Department of Telecommunications (DoT) 📌 WHAT IS THIS? Digital Communication Innovation Square (DCIS) supports startups and innovators in developing new digital communication technologies so India can strengthen its telecom sector and drive self‑reliance. 🎯 OBJECTIVES • To promote the ecosystem for research, design, development, proof of concept testing, Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) creation, pilot project and manufacturing i.e. complete value chain to make India a global hub for production of telecommunication equi pment and a centre for digital communication services. ✅ WHO CAN APPLY? • DPIIT recognised startups • Any Indian company incorporated under the Companies Act 1956/2013, primarily a Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) as defined in the MSME Act, 2006 having over 51% stakes by the Indian Citizen / NRI / OCI and Headquarter in India. • Individual Innovators will also be encouraged to apply (research & academic institutions can use this category to apply). However, release of fund shall be subjected to compliance of eligibility condition for either Startup or MSME before agreement signing. 💰 WHAT DO YOU GET? Milestone based support: • Startups up to ₹50 lakh • MSMEs up to ₹2 crore • Technology products requiring higher funding up to ₹10 crore 🚀 HOW TO APPLY • Apply on: https://dcis.dot.gov.in/ 🔗 KEY LINKS • Scheme guidelines: https://www.dot.gov.in/offerings/schemes-and-services/details/dcis- QjNzETMtQWa 💡 BEST SUITED FOR Prototyping to Pilot

text: PLAYBOOK OF GOVERNMENT SCHEMES AND INITIATIVES FOR STARTUPS Page 59 of 107 GREAT – Grant for Research & Entrepreneurship across Aspiring Innovators in Technical Textiles Ministry of Textiles (National Technical Textiles Mission) 📌 WHAT IS THIS? GREAT gives funding and incubator support to innovators and startups in technical textiles so they can turn prototypes into market-ready products and technologies. 🎯 OBJECTIVES • A scheme under the National Technical Textiles Mission (NTTM) to support technical-textile innovators and startups. It help young innovators, entrepreneurs and startups convert technical -textile prototypes into market-ready products/technologies. ✅ WHO CAN APPLY? • Individual innovators who are Indian citizens aged 21 years or above, incubated with an eligible incubator, and working on technical -textile innovation. • Startup companies incorporated as a private limited company, partnership firm or LLP, with turnover below ₹100 crore, not older than 5 years, and at least 51% Indian resident ownership/control. • Projects must relate to technical -textile areas such as agro -textiles, geo- textiles, medical textiles, protective textiles, smart textiles, high - performance fibres, sustainable textiles, composites, or indigenous machinery/equipment. 💰 WHAT DO YOU GET? • Grant-in-aid of normally up to ₹50 lakh per approved proposal for up to 18 months. • Funding is released milestone-wise, generally in 40:40:20 instalments. • Associated incubators receive an additional 10% of the sanctioned Government grant share for mentoring, due diligence and monitoring support. • Intellectual property generated remains with the innovator/startup or may be jointly shared with the incubator as per their agreement. 🚀 HOW TO APPLY • Apply online through the GREAT portal when applications are invited by NTTM/Ministry of Textiles. https://nttm.texmin.gov.in/StartupRegistration/StartupUserRegistration 🔗 KEY LINKS • GREAT Application Portal: https://nttm.texmin.gov.in/StartupRegistration/StartupUserRegistration • Scheme guidelines: http://www.nttm.texmin.gov.in/pdf/WhatsNew/Revised%20GREAT%20g uidelines.pdf 💡 BEST SUITED FOR Prototype to Commercialisation

text: PLAYBOOK OF GOVERNMENT SCHEMES AND INITIATIVES FOR STARTUPS Page 60 of 107 BHARATI – Bharat’s Hub for Agritech, Resilience, Advancement & Incubation for Export Innovation APEDA, Ministry of Commerce & Industry 📌 WHAT IS THIS? BHARATI helps agri-food and agritech startups become export-ready by giving them acceleration support, market access, and connections to the ecosystem needed to sell innovative products globally. 🎯 OBJECTIVES • It is a flagship initiative of Agricultural & Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) to strengthen India’s agri -food and processed food export ecosystem through innovation and startup acceleration. • It aims to empower agri-food and agri-tech startups and create new export opportunities, promote innovation in high-value agri-food products, export technologies, packaging, traceability, logistics, sustainability, and quality assurance. ✅ WHO CAN APPLY? • Agri-food startups developing innovative/high -value products for export, technology and service startups offering export-enabling solutions across the value chain. • Solution providers for SPS challenges, including startups, individual researchers, innovators and solo/self-employed entrepreneurs. • APEDA-registered exporters seeking to innovate or expand high -value product portfolios for international markets. • Farmer Producer Companies (FPCs) developing innovative/high -value agri-food products or SPS-related solutions. 💰 WHAT DO YOU GET? • Acceleration support covering product development, export readiness, regulatory compliance and market access. • Access to APEDA’s ecosystem, including industry bodies, state agricultural boards, universities, IITs/NITs and accelerators. • Support for innovative categories such as GI -tagged products, organic foods, superfoods, processed Indian foods, livestock products and AYUSH products. 🚀 HOW TO APPLY • Visit https://apeda.gov.in/bharati/ for more information. 🔗 KEY LINKS • BHARATI official portal: https://apeda.gov.in/bharati/ • Who can apply: https://apeda.gov.in/bharati/Who_Can_Apply.html 💡 BEST SUITED FOR Market Access

text: PLAYBOOK OF GOVERNMENT SCHEMES AND INITIATIVES FOR STARTUPS Page 61 of 107 S&T-PRISM – Promotion of Research & Innovation in Mining, Minerals & Recycling Sector Ministry of Mines 📌 WHAT IS THIS? S&T-PRISM helps early -stage startups in mining, minerals, metals, and recycling turn innovative ideas into working prototypes and pilot-ready solutions through funding and incubation support. 🎯 OBJECTIVES • The S&T-PRISM program aims to promote the ecosystem for research, design, development, proof of concept testing, IPR creation, pilot project and manufacturing i.e., complete value chain in mining, mineral processing, metallurgy and recycling sector. There are two components in the program: Startup Funding and Setting up Incubation Centres. ✅ WHO CAN APPLY? • Startups operating at the early stages in the mining and metal industry. 💰 WHAT DO YOU GET? • To Startups: Grant of up to ₹2 crore on milestone basis to startups showing capability, intent, and promise to be able to produce functional prototypes or to productize existing technologies. • To Incubators: Grant of up to ₹10 crore to incubators disbursed on milestone-basis. 🚀 HOW TO APPLY • Follow the instructions provided in the scheme guidelines https://mines.gov.in/admin/storage/app/uploads/655212bdb9e5b169987 7565.pdf 🔗 KEY LINKS • Operational Guidelines: https://mines.gov.in/admin/storage/app/uploads/655212bdb9e5b169987 7565.pdf 💡 BEST SUITED FOR Prototype to Pilot

text: PLAYBOOK OF GOVERNMENT SCHEMES AND INITIATIVES FOR STARTUPS Page 63 of 107 NIDHI – Entrepreneur in Residence (EIR) Department of Science and Technology (DST) 📌 WHAT IS THIS? NIDHI–EIR is a fellowship scheme that gives young people with startup ideas monthly financial support, workspace, and mentoring so they can turn their idea into a business 🎯 OBJECTIVES • The initiative NIDHI – Entrepreneur in Residence (EIR) is executed at selected NIDHI -Technology Business Incubator (TBI) known as Programme Executing Partner (PEP). These approved TBIs then select entrepreneurs under the programme pursuing a promising tech nology business idea. The objective is to encourage graduating students to take to entrepreneurship by providing support as a fellowship. ✅ WHO CAN APPLY? • The entrepreneur should be an Indian citizen. They should have completed minimum 4 years of formal full time undergraduate/post graduate education or 3 years degree or diploma program and have 2 - year full time work experience post degree or diploma. 💰 WHAT DO YOU GET? • Grant ranging from ₹10,000 to ₹30,000 per month for a period of 12 months, extendable up to 18 months. • The selected NIDHI-TBI will received a grant of ₹39.6 lakh each year, of which ₹36 lakh is to be provided to the NIDHI EIRs. • Co-working spaces for developing the idea into a marketable product. • Guidance from experienced, innovative and highly successful entrepreneurs on the business concept, strategy or venture and insight into specific industries or markets. 🚀 HOW TO APPLY The program is announced by the NIDHI-TBI locally. Applications by the EIR are to be submitted in a prescribed format 🔗 KEY LINKS • Website: https://nidhi.dst.gov.in/ • Guidelines: https://nidhi.dst.gov.in/nidhieir/ 💡 BEST SUITED FOR Ideation

text: PLAYBOOK OF GOVERNMENT SCHEMES AND INITIATIVES FOR STARTUPS Page 64 of 107 National Mission on Interdisciplinary Cyber- Physical Systems (NM-ICPS) – Technology Innovation Hubs Department of Science & Technology (DST) 📌 WHAT IS THIS? NM-ICPS Technology Innovation Hubs support people and startups working on advanced technologies by giving them funding and non-financial support to turn ideas into real products and businesses. 🎯 OBJECTIVES • The Department of Science & Technology (DST) is implementing multi- stakeholder National Mission on Interdisciplinary Cyber Physical System (NM-ICPS). The Mission works with all the concerned Ministries/ Departments to identify their technology needs, develop solutions and technical support. It aims at development of technology platforms to carry out R&D, Translational Research, Product Development, Incubating & Supporting Startups as well as Commercialization. Under NM -ICPS, 25 Technology Innovation Hubs (TIH) have been set up across the country. ✅ WHO CAN APPLY? • Under the 25 TIHs, individuals and entities including startups, students, entrepreneurs, and researchers, are invited to apply. 💰 WHAT DO YOU GET? • Eligible beneficiaries are provided with financial and non-financial support for research and development. 🚀 HOW TO APPLY • Technology Innovation Hubs release call for proposals periodically for different projects. Interested individuals/entities are advised to regularly check the call for proposals section on the NM-ICPS website. 🔗 KEY LINKS • Website: https://nmicps.in/ 💡 BEST SUITED FOR Prototype to Scaling

text: PLAYBOOK OF GOVERNMENT SCHEMES AND INITIATIVES FOR STARTUPS Page 65 of 107 National Initiative for Developing and Harnessing Innovations - Technology Business Incubator (NIDHI-TBI) Department of Science and Technology 📌 WHAT IS THIS? NIDHI-TBI supports institutions in setting up incubators so they can help technology-based ideas grow into startups. 🎯 OBJECTIVES • The initiative aims to convert technology -based innovations into startups by supporting institutions in setting up Technology Business Incubators (TBIs). The initiative provides support for non -recurring and recurring expenses of TBIs. ✅ WHO CAN APPLY? • Host Institute (HI) such as Academic/Technical/R&D Institutes and other institutions with a proven track record in promotion of technology -based entrepreneurship, with adequate expertise and infrastructure to support incubation activities, or • A legal entity registered in India with the clear purpose and objective of promoting research, innovation, and entrepreneurial ecosystem. Not -for- profit legal entity registered as a society/trust/section 8 company 💰 WHAT DO YOU GET? • Non-recurring capital: For publicly funded institutes, 100% support can be provided for renovation/furnishing. In case of other institutes, certain percentage of the total cost (excluding land & building) will be provided. • Recurring: Out of the total recurring expenditure incurred by the NIDHI - TBI against the approved amount, following mode of funding by DST would be followed on actual recurring expenditure. 🚀 HOW TO APPLY • Proposal is to be submitted in the prescribed proforma available at https://nidhi.dst.gov.in/ 🔗 KEY LINKS • Operational Guidelines: https://nidhi.dst.gov.in/nidhitbi/ 💡 BEST SUITED FOR Incubation

text: PLAYBOOK OF GOVERNMENT SCHEMES AND INITIATIVES FOR STARTUPS Page 66 of 107 NIDHI - Inclusive-Technology Business Incubator (i-TBI) Department of Science and Technology (DST) 📌 WHAT IS THIS? NIDHI i-TBI supports institutions in underserved regions to set up incubators so local innovators and startups can get the space, funding, and support needed to build new ventures. 🎯 OBJECTIVES • The NIDHI i -TBI initiative aims to support institutions in regions where innovation and startup incubation ecosystem is at nascent stages and ‘Inclusive TBI’ can play a vital role in normalizing resources and value creation across the country. The i-TBI would create a culture of innovation and entrepreneurship in the Host Institute (HI) and nearby geographies. ✅ WHO CAN APPLY? • The HI is to provide up to 10,000 square feet (minimum 7,000 square feet) of built-up space to host i-TBI in the campus. • The HI shall agree to establish separate Section 8 company to professionally manage the i -TBI and will execute a lease agreement between HI and new (Section 8) entity, to lease the space earmarked for the i-TBI to new entity at no cost or at minimum rate for 10 years or beyond. • The i -TBI should be capable of accommodating at least 30 innovative ventures/startups. 💰 WHAT DO YOU GET? • DST will provide the necessary capital fund to establish the infrastructure of i-TBI. • The i-TBI is provided with a maximum funding of ₹5 crore over a period of 3 years. • Funding for non-recurring expenditure: • For private institutions – 50:50 share between DST and HI • For public institutions – 75:25 share between DST and HI, respectively. • The ignition grant shall be for development of prototype/products. 🚀 HOW TO APPLY Visit the online portal i.e., https://nidhi.dst.gov.in/ 🔗 KEY LINKS • Website:

text: PLAYBOOK OF GOVERNMENT SCHEMES AND INITIATIVES FOR STARTUPS Page 67 of 107 NIDHI-Accelerator Department of Science and Technology (DST) 📌 WHAT IS THIS? NIDHI-Accelerator helps incubators run short, intensive programs that give promising startups mentoring, networks, and demo -day support so they can grow faster. 🎯 OBJECTIVES • The umbrella programme ‘National Initiative for Developing and Harnessing Innovations (NIDHI)’ developed in 2016 aims to nurture the innovation ecosystem in India. Key components of the NIDHI program are outlined in the following sections. • NIDHI Accelerators are positioned as post-incubation initiatives linked with the existing incubators to supplement, complement the scaling up of the startup value chain. Under the programme, DST encourages its existing TBIs and other incubators to extensively adopt and evolve the accelerator mode. It aims to fast track the growth of potential startups through rigorous mentoring and networking support in a short span through existing TBIs. ✅ WHO CAN APPLY? • TBIs previously funded or currently funded by DST or any other Central or State government with a minimum 3 years in existence, having nurtured and incubated at least 20 startups in multiple domains. 💰 WHAT DO YOU GET? • Contribution towards the overall budget for running accelerators shall not exceed ₹40 lakh per program of one cohort. It is further divided into two categories: • Accelerator Program with a maximum limit of ₹30 lakh, that includes manpower, logistics, travel, mentoring, infrastructure, training, and all other cost. • Demo Day Award with maximum budget of ₹10 lakh where top 3 to 5 startups of the batch are awarded on the basis of their performance/ achievements during the accelerator program. 🚀 HOW TO APPLY • Visit the online portal https://nidhi.dst.gov.in/ 🔗 KEY LINKS • Website: https://nidhi.dst.gov.in/ • Guidelines: https://nidhi.dst.gov.in/schemes- programmes/nidhiaccelerator/ 💡 BEST SUITED FOR Acceleration

text: PLAYBOOK OF GOVERNMENT SCHEMES AND INITIATIVES FOR STARTUPS Page 68 of 107 NIDHI-Centres of Excellence (CoE) Department of Science and Technology (DST) 📌 WHAT IS THIS? NIDHI-CoE supports established incubators in building world-class facilities and services so that high-potential technology startups can turn innovations into scalable businesses. 🎯 OBJECTIVES • Under NIDHI-Centres of Excellence (CoE), the DST empowers incubators to provide an enabling environment for the growth of technology startups to enhance the prospects of their success. The NIDHI -CoE proposes to strengthen existing capacities of STEP/TBIs and support potential startups with different pursuits and practices in transferring technolo gical innovations into marketable products/high -growth companies. DST has priority areas for supporting NIDHI-CoEs. ✅ WHO CAN APPLY? • Existing incubator with incubation experience of at least 5 years. • For non-academic institution, it should be a legal entity registered in India with the clear purpose of promoting research, innovation, and entrepreneurial ecosystem. • The financial support for establishing a NIDHI-CoE would be extended to a not -for-profit legal entity registered as a Society/Trust/Section 8 company. • The host institution should be in existence for at least 8 years. This will not apply to entities created by the Central or State governments. 💰 WHAT DO YOU GET? • An enhanced support of maximum of ₹50 crore in 5 years. • Public funded institutions: Would be eligible for 100% support including building • Private institution: Eligible for recurring support of ₹20 crore and a maximum of ₹1 crore for equipment • The support would include design/prototype development & Validation Centres along with the Patent Facilitation centres, state -of-the-art technology based TBI facilities to accommodate minimum 100 startups and an accelerator for 10 high potential startups. 🚀 HOW TO APPLY • Proposals are received throughout the year. It is focused on supporting Biotech, Medtech, Healthtech, Pharma, Agritech & Cleantech startups to raise their angel round from Angel Investors who brin g deep domain expertise. ✅ WHO CAN APPLY? • Startups and entrepreneurs operating in Biotech, Medtech, Healthtech, Pharma, Cleantech & Agritech sectors. 💰 WHAT DO YOU GET? • BioAngels provides financial incentives, mentoring, and market access. • It aims to fuel the ecosystem through interactions with high -quality investors and industry leaders, whilst emphasizing a strong operational focus, frameworks, processes, and governance. • The inclusive group of ecosystem stakeholders at BioAngels comprises HNIs, angel investors, family offices, strategic investors, corporates, and VCs. 🚀 HOW TO APPLY • Apply here: https://bioangels.vc/ 🔗 KEY LINKS • Website: https://bioangels.vc/about-us/ 💡 BEST SUITED FOR Early-stage

text: PLAYBOOK OF GOVERNMENT SCHEMES AND INITIATIVES FOR STARTUPS Page 70 of 107 BioNEST Programme Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC), Department of Biotechnology 📌 WHAT IS THIS? The BioNEST program enables certain entities (educational institutions, incubators etc.) to create globally competent bio -incubation facilities for targeted scaling up of biotech startup ecosystem. 🎯 OBJECTIVES • The BioNEST (Bioincubators Nurturing Entrepreneurship for Scaling Technologies) program is supported by BIRAC to create globally competent bio-incubation facilities across the country in order to facilitate the targeted scaling up of biotech startup ecosystem. • To provide entrepreneurs with incubation space with shared access to high end infrastructure, specialized and advanced equipment • To provide entrepreneurs with business mentorship, IP, egal and regulatory guidance, and networking opportunities. ✅ WHO CAN APPLY? • Relevant incorporated Indian legal entities including: Educational institutions, Business Incubators, Biotech -Parks, State government Science and Technology bodies, Biotech State Councils, Research Hospitals. 💰 WHAT DO YOU GET? • Grant-in-aid, based on the need and scope of the project as adjudged by the BioNEST committee. • BIRAC funding to cater to refurbishment/ renovation of space, equipment, furniture and operational cost. 🚀 HOW TO APPLY • Interested applicants may submit their applications online via https://www.birac.nic.in/desc_new.php?id=1120. 🔗 KEY LINKS • Website: https://www.birac.nic.in/desc_new.php?id=1120 • Operational Guidelines: https://www.birac.nic.in/webcontent/1707480045_BioNEST_Guidelines.p df 💡 BEST SUITED FOR Incubation

text: PLAYBOOK OF GOVERNMENT SCHEMES AND INITIATIVES FOR STARTUPS Page 71 of 107 Biotechnology Industry Partnership Programme (BIPP) Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC), Department of Biotechnology 📌 WHAT IS THIS? Under BIPP, the Government offers support to startups in partnership with industries for research in frontier futuristic technology areas. 🎯 OBJECTIVES • The Biotechnology Industry Partnership Programme (BIPP) is a government partnership with industries for support on a cost sharing basis for research in frontier futuristic technology areas. It is focused on IP creation with ownership retained by Indian industry and wherever relevant, by collaborating scientists. ✅ WHO CAN APPLY? Single company or consortia of companies incorporated under the Companies Act, 2013; or Limited Liability Partnership (LLP) incorporated under the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008, jointly with or without the following: • Public/private university/colleges in India • National research laboratories • Not-for-profit private research labs/societies/foundation/NGO 💰 WHAT DO YOU GET? • One time grant-in-aid (subject to a maximum of ₹50 lakh) is provided by BIRAC to those startups which have not received grant -in-aid under any scheme of BIRAC in past. • If the startup has received funding from BIRAC before, BIRAC contribution will be restricted to a maximum of 70% of the total budget of the respective entity (Minimum 30% of the total budget will be contributed by the respective Company. 🚀 HOW TO APPLY • Call for Applications are announced twice a year (1st April – 15th May; 1st September – 15th October) • Proposals are required to be submitted online only. Call for proposals and application link can be found on the BIRAC website: https://birac.nic.in/cfp.php 🔗 KEY LINKS • Detailed guidelines: https://birac.nic.in/webcontent/1745298172_BIPP_scheme_guidelines_1 6_04_2025.pdf 💡 BEST SUITED FOR Validation to Commercialisation

E-YUVA supports students and young researchers with funding, mentoring, and incubation support so they can turn useful biotech ideas into real solutions or startups. 🎯 OBJECTIVES • E-YUVA was initiated by BIRAC to promote a culture of applied research and need-oriented (societal or industry) entrepreneurial innovation among young students and researchers. It is implemented through dedicated hubs called E-Yuva Centers (EYCs), housed within the University/Institute set up and mentored by a BIRAC BioNEST supported bio -incubator. The Scheme provides support under two categories: BIRAC’s Innovation Fellows (post -graduates and above), and BIRAC’s E -YUVA Fellows (undergraduate students). ✅ WHO CAN APPLY? • Innovation Fellows: An Indian Student who has completed Masters/ Ph.D. in any discipline. • E-YUVA Fellows: Indian students pursuing under graduation in any domain. 💰 WHAT DO YOU GET? • The Scheme provides funding support – through fellowship and research grants. • Monthly fellowship grant provided under the Scheme ranges between ₹30,000-₹50,000. Annual research grant range between ₹3 lakh to ₹5 lakh. • Technical and business mentoring, exposure to bioincubation model, orientation to entrepreneurial culture etc. is also provided to students. 🚀 HOW TO APPLY • Two Calls for Applications announced in a year. • Online applications are to be submitted through the BIRAC website: https://birac.nic.in • The shortlisted applicants/teams are called for a presentation before a Technical Expert Committee along with BIRAC nominee at respective EYCs 🔗 KEY LINKS • Website: https://birac.nic.in/e_yuva.php • Operational Guidelines: https://birac.nic.in/webcontent/1658838527_EYUVA_Guideline_Version_ 1.1.pdf 💡 BEST SUITED FOR Ideation (Students)

text: PLAYBOOK OF GOVERNMENT SCHEMES AND INITIATIVES FOR STARTUPS Page 73 of 107 Students Innovations for Translation & Advancement of Research Explorations (SITARE) Department of Biotechnology (DBT) 📌 WHAT IS THIS? SITARE supports student innovators in biotechnology with funding, training, and mentoring so they can turn promising research ideas into practical solutions or startups. 🎯 OBJECTIVES • Students Innovations for Translation & Advancement of Research Explorations (SITARE) Scheme aims to promote and support innovative student projects in the area of biotechnology. • The scheme has two components, SITARE -Gandhian Young Technological Innovation Award Grant (SITARE -GYTI), and SITARE - Appreciation Grant. ✅ WHO CAN APPLY? • SITARE-GYTI: An Indian Student pursuing Ph.D./Masters in any discipline. • SITARE-Appreciation Grant: Students pursuing undergraduate programme in any discipline, preferably from Tier II/Tier III cities and aspirational districts within India. 💰 WHAT DO YOU GET? • SITARE-GYTI: Innovative student projects receive funding support of up to ₹15 lakh each for projects with commercial potential leading to creation of biotech startups. • SITARE-Appreciation Grant: Students selected to attend Biotech Innovation Ignition School (BIIS) workshops are eligible to receive funding support of up to ₹1 lakh each, followed by training and mentoring. 🚀 HOW TO APPLY • For SITARE -GYTI: The call for application opens once a year in August/September for 45 -60 days. Proposals shall be submitted online only. • SITARE-Appreciation Grant: Applications need to be submitted online only. Call for applications are invited against advertisement by SITARE Partner 🔗 KEY LINKS • To apply, visit https://www.birac.nic.in/ and login as a registered user. • Guidelines: https://birac.nic.in/webcontent/1584008982_SITARE_Scheme_Guideline s.pdf 💡 BEST SUITED FOR Ideation to Translation (Students)

text: PLAYBOOK OF GOVERNMENT SCHEMES AND INITIATIVES FOR STARTUPS Page 74 of 107 Promoting Academic Research Conversion to Enterprise (PACE) Department of Biotechnology (DBT) 📌 WHAT IS THIS? PACE helps academic institutions turn important research into early -stage products and then supports industry partnerships to validate and take those innovations closer to real-world use. 🎯 OBJECTIVES • The PACE (Promoting Academic Research Conversion to Enterprise) encourages academia to develop technology/product (up to PoC stage) of societal/national importance (under Academic Innovation Research or AIR), and its subsequent validation by an industrial partner (under Contract Research Scheme or CRS. ✅ WHO CAN APPLY? • For AIR: Academia (Public or Private Institute, University, NGO, or Research Foundation) with a well-established support system for research shall be the primary applicant. Collaboration with Industry/LLP is optional in this component. • For CRS: Mandatory collaboration with Industry/LLP is needed. The Industry collaborator must have a minimum of 51% of the shares of the Company held by Indian Citizens holding Indian passport. 💰 WHAT DO YOU GET? • PACE provides for BIRAC contribution of up to 100% of the project cost. • Financial support under AIR: Total cost of the project must not exceed ₹50 lakh (non-recurring cost must not exceed 10% of the total cost) • Financial support under CRS: Funding in the form of grant is provided to both academic as well as industrial partners. There is no ceiling to the funding under CRS. 🚀 HOW TO APPLY • Call for Applications are announced twice a year (1st April – 15th May; and 1st September – 15th October). Besides two regular calls, BIRAC may also announce need -based additional calls whose terms and conditions would be worked out separately and described in their respective RFPs. 🔗 KEY LINKS • Website: https://birac.nic.in/desc_new.php?id=286 • Operational Guidelines: https://birac.nic.in/webcontent/1613355528_PACE_scheme_document_ 15_02_2021.pdf
